title: FAQ - RSO Recognition Process
text:
FAQ - RSO Recognition Process (USC Campus Activities)

New organizations: New RSO applications open in October for spring recognition. Fall processing is only for previously recognized RSOs. New RSOs can't get fall recognition in their first year. Requirements: at least 5 officers, 1 full-time USC staff or faculty advisor, and at least 10 currently enrolled student members. Officers must be currently enrolled students. Constitution: organizations must use the required template; the 2025-26 template is on the RSO Recognition page. Training: officers must complete all required modules before the deadline; certificates must be from the current academic year; advisors must complete Advisor Training as of Fall 2024. Good standing: the RSO and all officers must be in good standing with the Office of Community Expectations and EEO-TIX. Prior unrecognized behavior that conflicts with the USC Student Handbook or Student Commitment can lead to denial. Existing groups are listed on EngageSC under 'Groups.' Groups denied for past conduct may reapply in a future year, but only if they stop presenting as an RSO and stop using RSO benefits, and they must avoid future conduct violations.

Annual recognition (current RSOs): Since 2024-25, all RSOs must reapply each year; prior recognition does not guarantee future recognition. The same officer, advisor, member, constitution, training, and good-standing requirements apply each year. Recognition runs from August through June 30. Officers and advisors must retake training each year. Incomplete applications are not considered; the group must wait for the next cycle. RSOs cannot operate while their applications are pending. USC recognition must come first and must be renewed annually before school or department recognition. USC can revoke, limit, or suspend recognition for reasons including incomplete renewals, hazing, fronting, theft, or other Handbook violations. Groups that lose recognition face a multi-year wait and must stop all activities and RSO benefits during that period.

Reestablishing a paused organization: Groups that were dormant or missed a cycle should complete the Google Form linked on the page; Campus Activities will follow up after the fall cycle. Groups that lost recognition after a conduct case should email stuacts@usc.edu.

Appeals: Denials can be appealed to the AVP for Student Culture and Community, or a designee, within ten business days of the decision. Appeals must be a written statement of no more than 5 pages, emailed to Campus Activities. The appeal decision is final for that year. Groups under a disciplinary sanction that suspended or revoked recognition cannot apply or appeal. Only approved groups may access RSO benefits.

RSO advisors: Advisors must be full-time USC staff or faculty with active USC email and SSO credentials. Advisors are the main University contact and must know the RSO's activities, university policies, and their role as a Campus Security Authority (CSA). Required annual items: RSO Advisor training on the Reach360 platform; CSA training assigned through Trojan Learn (accessible via the Employee Gateway under 'My Transcript'); review and signature of the Commitment to Community document. Advisors receive an email after the application closes with links to the training and an RSO Advisor Requirements form. Campus Activities will announce advisor deadlines separately.

Contact: Email stuacts@usc.edu (general questions, appeals, reestablishment); the footer lists campact@usc.edu. Phone: 213-740-5649. Office: Campus Activities, Steven & Kathryn Sample Hall (SKS) 410, 3607 Trousdale Parkway, Los Angeles, CA 90089. Hours: Monday-Friday, 9:00 am-5:00 pm.
